title: 1PUX v3 export.data (official profile)
description: JSON Schema for the ``export.data`` entry of a 1PUX ZIP archive. Intersection of the fields the official v3 exporter emits and the official v3 importer consumes. This is the default round-trip profile: it deliberately omits passkeys (the exporter path does not emit them) and local-only metadata such as appIds. See docs/schema/README.md for the ZIP layout and the companion ``export.attributes`` schema.
$comment: Recovered from the shipped 1Password desktop core (op_import_export::models::translation::onepux::v2/v3). Primary importer visitors (nm addresses): 0x4740aa0 (ItemDetails), 0x4740d10 (ItemOverview), 0x4740760 (DetailSection), 0x47414a0 (DetailSectionField), 0x4740830 (DocumentAttributes), 0x47412e0 (LoginField), 0x4740370 (OverviewUrl), 0x4740fd0 (SectionFieldValue), 0x492fc80 (InputTraits). Required-field evidence: ItemOverview.subtitle missing-field call at 0x4587208; DetailSectionField title/value/id/guarded at 0x43e01xx; DocumentAttributes fileName/decryptedSize at 0x4324f87/0x432505d; InputTraits keyboard/correction/capitalization via 0x492fc80. Main exporter path: 0x4c4fb70 (onepux::export closure) and 0x6173620 (ItemDetails::from). File entries use ``files/<documentId>__<fileName>`` (two underscores); the format string is at 0x11f79ac, its call site is 0x4c52c4a, and the importer lookup is 0x4535aae.

ExportAttributes.description: Contents of the ``export.attributes`` ZIP entry. This object is not part of ``export.data``; it is documented here because both files belong to the same 1PUX archive.

version.description: 1PUX schema version. The v3 exporter writes 3.

timestamp.description: Export creation time. Recovered from the v3 exporter, which writes ``timestamp`` rather than the ``createdAt`` spelling used by the public format documentation.

ExportAttributes.$comment: Recovered from op_import_export::models::translation::onepux::v3. The public 1PUX page shows createdAt, while the shipped exporter writes timestamp. No createdAt property is declared here because the importer's acceptance of that spelling was not proven from the binary.

accountName.description: Display name of the account/team as shown by the official exporter.

avatar.description: Filename of the account avatar inside the ZIP ``files/`` directory. An empty string means no avatar. onedecrypt clears this field in canonical profiles because it does not export the avatar blob.

uuid.description: 1Password object identifier. The official exporter writes the usual 26-character lowercase base32 identifier; the importer treats it as an opaque string, so this schema does not impose a pattern.

domain.description: Account sign-in URL, for example https://my.1password.com/.

uuid.description: 1Password object identifier. The official exporter writes the usual 26-character lowercase base32 identifier; the importer treats it as an opaque string, so this schema does not impose a pattern.

desc.description: Vault description; empty string when not set.

avatar.description: Filename of the vault avatar inside the ZIP ``files/`` directory. An empty string means no avatar. onedecrypt clears this field in canonical profiles because it does not export the avatar blob.

type.description: Vault type. P = Personal/Private, E = Everyone/Shared, U = user-created vault. The exporter can also emit T (team), S (shared), G (guest), M (managed) and D (default). onedecrypt canonical profiles map values outside P/E/U to U.

uuid.description: 1Password object identifier. The official exporter writes the usual 26-character lowercase base32 identifier; the importer treats it as an opaque string, so this schema does not impose a pattern.

favIndex.description: 0 means not a favorite; greater than 0 means favorite.

state.description: Item state. The v3 serializer maps 0, 1, 2 to active, archived and deleted; the importer accepts all three. onedecrypt's official/exporter policy skips trashed items during extraction, so those profiles normally contain only active/archived even though the format can represent deleted.

categoryUuid.description: Item category identifier. Known values include 001 Login, 002 Credit Card, 003 Secure Note, 004 Identity, 005 Password, 006 Document, 100 Software License, 114 SSH Key and 115 Crypto Wallet.

Item.$comment: v3 InnerVaultItem field order: uuid, favIndex, createdAt, updatedAt, state, categoryUuid, details, overview.

ItemDetails.description: Item details (``items[].details``). The official exporter always writes loginFields, sections and passwordHistory, possibly empty.

notesPlain.description: Free-form notes; markdown formatting is preserved.

password.description: Password value for Password items (categoryUuid 005), which have no loginFields.

ItemDetails.$comment: ItemDetails is the v2 struct reused by v3. The importer field visitor accepts htmlForm, loginFields, notesPlain, sections, passwordHistory, password, passkey and documentAttributes. The passkey value is deserialized through force_none and discarded, so only the raw full profile preserves it.

ItemOverview.description: Item overview (``items[].overview``). The official exporter emits the canonical keys; the importer additionally accepts several legacy spellings.

title.description: Item title shown in the item list.

urls.description: All URLs associated with the item.

ps.description: Password strength score emitted by 1Password. The UI normally shows 0-100; the field is not range-checked by the importer.

subtitle.description: Generated subtitle, usually the username or a short summary.

icons.description: Custom icon map keyed by icon slot, or null when the item has no custom icon. The exporter writes referenced files under ``files/``; onedecrypt omits custom icon blobs.

locations.description: Saved locations associated with the item.

b5UserUuid.description: B5 user UUID. The official importer accepts both this spelling and ``b5UserUUID``.

watchtowerExclusions.description: Watchtower exclusions. The exporter writes null when there are none, otherwise an object of boolean exclusion flags.

migrationDestination.description: Migration destination emitted by the official exporter.

ItemOverview.$comment: ItemOverview importer field list: ainfo, subtitle, b5UserUUID, b5UserUuid, icons, URLs, urls, tags, title, url, ps, pbe, pgrng, passkeyId, passkey, MigrationDestination, migrationDestination, watchtowerExclusions, shortcut, locations. subtitle and url are non-Option Strings; appIds is local-only. passkey/passkeyId are accepted only through force_none and are not imported.

ItemShortcut.description: Keyboard shortcut associated with the item. The exporter models this as a struct with ``value`` and ``case_sensitive`` rather than a bare string.

WatchtowerExclusions.description: Watchtower exclusions object. The exporter writes null instead of this object when there are no exclusions; each boolean field selects one Watchtower check.

compromised.description: Whether the compromised Watchtower check is excluded.

vulnerable.description: Whether the vulnerable Watchtower check is excluded.

reused.description: Whether the reused Watchtower check is excluded.

weak.description: Whether the weak Watchtower check is excluded.

unsecured.description: Whether the unsecured Watchtower check is excluded.

inactiveMfa.description: Whether the inactiveMfa Watchtower check is excluded.

expiring.description: Whether the expiring Watchtower check is excluded.

lastpass.description: Whether the lastpass Watchtower check is excluded.

wrongAccount.description: Whether the wrongAccount Watchtower check is excluded.

passkeyAvailable.description: Whether the passkeyAvailable Watchtower check is excluded.

duplicateItem.description: Whether the duplicateItem Watchtower check is excluded.

conflictingShortcut.description: Whether the conflictingShortcut Watchtower check is excluded.

MigrationDestination.description: Migration destination emitted by the exporter for items that were migrated from another account.

LoginField.description: A web-form/login field. The official exporter writes ``value``, ``id``, ``name`` and ``fieldType``; ``designation`` is optional.

id.description: Field identifier; may be empty for template-driven fields.

name.description: HTML form field name; may be empty.

fieldType.description: Free-form HTML input type. The official importer does not constrain this to the T/E/U/N/P/A/TEL list shown in older documentation; real vaults contain other values such as D or C.

designation.description: Semantic role of a login field. At most one field should be ``username`` and at most one ``password``.

LoginField.$comment: ItemDetails.loginFields is Vec<LoginField>. The importer's visit_str accepts value/id/name/fieldType/type/designation.

title.description: Section heading shown to the user.

name.description: Stable section identifier within the item.

fields.description: Fields in this section. The official exporter always writes an array, possibly empty.

hideAddAnotherField.description: Whether the UI should hide the 'add another field' affordance.

DetailSection.$comment: DetailSection importer fields: title, name, fields, hideAddAnotherField. title is required by the importer.

DetailSectionField.description: One field inside a detail section. The official exporter emits long-form keys (title/id/value/...); short B5 keys are not part of the canonical profiles.

id.description: Field identifier. Uniqueness is not guaranteed; template fields use template-provided identifiers.

dontGenerate.description: Whether the password generator is disabled.

indexAtSource.description: Original index of the field in its source form/section.

DetailSectionField.$comment: DetailSectionField importer fields: title, id, value, indexAtSource, guarded, multiline, clipboardFilter, dontGenerate, inputTraits, placeholder. keyboard/correction live inside inputTraits, not at the field level. The official exporter writes value/guarded/multiline/dontGenerate/inputTraits for every field.

InputTraits.description: Keyboard/autocorrection hints for a section field (``details.sections[].fields[].inputTraits``). The importer's DetailSectionFieldInputTraits struct has three non-Option enum fields; the official exporter always writes all three.
InputTraits.$comment: DetailSectionFieldInputTraits (0x492fc80) requires keyboard, correction and capitalization; absent values default to 'default'.

DocumentAttributes.description: A document reference. Document items carry this object at ``details.documentAttributes``; section attachments carry it at ``details.sections[].fields[].value.file``.

fileName.description: Original file name. The ZIP entry is ``files/<documentId>__<fileName>`` (two underscores).

documentId.description: Document identifier. Together with fileName it forms the ZIP entry name. The importer models this as Option<Uuid>.

DocumentAttributes.$comment: DocumentAttributes serializer (0x4723be0) always writes fileName and decryptedSize; documentId is Option<Uuid>. The deserializer also accepts signingKey, decryptedSize/unencryptedSize, encryptedSize, integrityHash, encryptionKey, nonce and uti.

DetailHtmlForm.description: Saved web-form metadata (``details.htmlForm``). The official exporter emits ``htmlId``; the importer accepts both ``htmlId`` and ``htmlID``.

htmlMethod.description: HTML form method, for example POST.

htmlAction.description: HTML form action URL or path.

htmlId.description: HTML form id attribute. The shipped exporter writes ``htmlId`` (lower-case d).

PasswordHistoryEntry.description: One previous password. Entries are ordered oldest first; ``time`` is the moment that value stopped being current.

OverviewUrl.description: One entry of ``overview.urls``. The canonical spelling uses ``label``/``url``/``mode``.

label.description: Display label for the URL; empty string when unlabeled.

mode.description: 1Password URL matching mode. The exporter's ``From<ItemUrl>`` conversion writes the lowercase ItemUrlMode spelling.

ItemLocation.description: Saved location entry. The importer's ItemLocation enum has one externally tagged variant, ``Gps``.

location.description: Optional coordinate payload; the official exporter may write null.

IconKey.description: Opaque icon reference. The official exporter can emit custom icon metadata and write the referenced file under ``files/``. onedecrypt omits custom icons because their blobs are not part of the local export cache.
